working: The Etard reaction (toluene + CrO2Cl2 in CS2, then H3O+) gives benzaldehyde, so P = PhCHO. Checking each option: (1) benzaldehyde is not an acid, so no effervescence with NaHCO3. (2) Friedel–Crafts acylation with CH3COCl gives acetophenone, not benzaldehyde. (3) The white precipitate with bromine water is characteristic of phenol, not benzaldehyde. (4) Rosenmund reduction of benzoyl chloride (H2, Pd/BaSO4) gives benzaldehyde, which is correct.
